page.query: What is Community as a Service?
page.title: What Is Community as a Service? Buyer Guide
page.description: Learn what Community as a Service covers, which platforms fit, how to split in-house and outsourced work, pricing models, launch timelines, and metrics that prove value.
page.h1: What Is Community as a Service?
page.definition: Community as a Service is an outsourced operating model in which a specialist partner helps a company design, launch, operate, measure, and improve an owned community across platforms such as Discord, Slack, or Circle while the brand retains strategy and voice approval.
page.quick_answer: Treat community as a product: define the six components, assign owners for strategy and brand voice, outsource moderation and programming, and review metrics monthly on a ninety-day plan.

sections.h2: What does a Community as a Service engagement cover?

blocks.p: A full engagement spans six components reviewed monthly: strategy and governance, platform configuration, onboarding and activation, programming and events, moderation and safety, and reporting and iteration.

ul: Strategy and governance sets purpose, rules, and escalation paths
Platform configuration builds spaces, roles, and integrations
Onboarding and activation designs welcome flows and first-value moments
Programming and events schedules AMAs, office hours, and peer groups
Moderation and safety covers coverage hours, triage, and crisis playbooks
Reporting and iteration tracks health signals and feeds the next cycle

sections.h2: Which platforms work with this model?

blocks.p: The model is platform-agnostic; the partner configures and operates on the system your audience already uses or the one that fits your security and scale needs.

sections.h2: How do you decide what to keep in-house versus outsource?

blocks.p: Draw a hard line at strategy, brand voice approval, and product decisions; everything else can sit with the partner.

ul: Keep in-house: strategy, brand voice approval, product decisions
Outsource: moderation, member support, programming, onboarding, reporting

sections.h2: What does the pricing structure look like?

blocks.p: Pricing is scoped by coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk, and programming cadence; there is no published rate card.
West Peek Productions quotes Community as a Service by scope and does not publish a fixed price; send the scope for a quote.

sections.h2: How long does it take to launch a managed community?

blocks.p: A first plan runs ninety days: long enough to see a trend, short enough to change course.

ol: Weeks one to two: intake, audit, and component design
Weeks three to four: platform setup, welcome flow, and moderation playbooks
Week five: soft launch with founding members
Week six: public launch and first programming cycle
Months two to three: iterate on data, add sub-groups, scale moderation

sections.h2: What metrics should you track to prove value?

blocks.p: Owned audience beats rented reach: count email subscribers and community members, not only followers.

ul: Retention at thirty, sixty, ninety days

faq.q: Can we start with only moderation and add programming later?
faq.a: Yes. The model is modular; you can begin with coverage hours and safety playbooks, then layer in events, onboarding flows, and reporting as budget and member volume grow.

faq.q: Do we need to migrate platforms to use a managed service?
faq.a: No. The partner works on your existing platform — Discord, Slack, Circle, or another — and only recommends a move if the current tool cannot support your safety or scale requirements.

faq.q: How is crisis handling defined in the contract?
faq.a: Escalation paths, response-time SLAs, and communication templates are documented in the governance component and rehearsed during onboarding so the partner can act without waiting for approval.

faq.q: What internal resources must we allocate?
faq.a: Assign a single stakeholder for strategy sign-off, brand voice reviews, and product feedback; the partner handles daily operations, moderation queues, programming logistics, and monthly reporting.

faq.q: How do we measure ROI beyond vanity metrics?
faq.a: Track support ticket deflection, referral-driven sign-ups, sales-qualified leads sourced from community, and content reuse rate across marketing channels; review these monthly against the ninety-day plan.
